# Initialisation
First access required modules.
```{julia}
using Compose, Colors, Measures
import EpidemicsCFTP, Gadfly
epi = EpidemicsCFTP ;
```

A laconic description of the `julia` package `Compose.jl` 
(the graphics package used for these figures)
is provided at 
<https://giovineitalia.github.io/Compose.jl/latest/>.
Further useful information can be found in 
<https://shashi.biz/ijulia-notebooks/funcgeo/>.

Basic simulation parameters are the `population` size 
and the `duration` (assumes epidemic simulation commences at time `0`).
Note that (trivial) labelling issues arise if `population > MAXPOP=20`.
```{julia}
const population = 5 ;
const duration   = 2 ;

const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if population > MAXPOP
  error("`population` exceeds `$(MAXPOP)`: modify code indexing time-lines!")
end ;
```

We now set up and establish graphics size, coordinates, and drawing region.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 3.25inch) ;

coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population, 
                      leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch) ;
region      = (context(), rectangle(), fill(colorant"bisque"), fillopacity(0.3)) ;
```


# Basic image template elements
First construct the time axis, with tick marks at integer times.
Note, here and following,  careful use of graphics area units (`cx`, `cy`) 
```{julia}
tic       = -0.2cy
step      = 10^floor(Int, log10(duration))
xht       = 0.5cy # 0cy + 0.25inch
labellocs = [(x)cx for x in 0:duration]

tic_loc1  = [(((x)cx,xht), ((x)cx, xht+tic))    for x in 0:1.0step:duration]
tic_loc2  = [(((x)cx,xht), ((x)cx, xht+tic))    for x in 0:0.5step:duration]
tic_loc3  = [(((x)cx,xht), ((x)cx, xht+0.5tic)) for x in 0:0.1step:duration]

time_axis = (context(),
   (context(), text(labellocs, [xht + 0.25inch], ["$i" for i in 0:duration], 
      [hcenter], [vcenter]), fontsize(7pt), font("TimesRoman"), ),
   (context(), line([(0cx, xht), ((duration)cx, xht)]),
      stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.5mm) ),
   (context(), line(tic_loc1), stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.2mm)),
   (context(), line(tic_loc2), stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.1mm)),
   (context(), line(tic_loc3), stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.1mm)), ) ;
```


Now build the time-lines, labelled by circled integers.

::: {.callout-caution}
The definition of `circlabels` below needs to be changed if `population > MAXPOP=20`,
as unicode then runs out of circled integers!
(Figure out how to use 
one of the many ideas in <https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/7032/good-way-to-make-textcircled-numbers#>.)
:::

```{julia}
circlabels   = [string(Char(0x00002460+i-1)) for i in 1:population]

lines        = (context(),
  (context(), text([0cx-0.25inch], [(k)cy for k in 1:population], circlabels,
      [hleft], [vcenter]), fontsize(10pt), font("TimesRoman"), ),
  (context(), line([[(0cx, (k)cy), ((duration)cx, (k)cy)] for k in 1:population]), 
      stroke("grey"), linewidth(0.5mm), ), ) ;
```

Finally we build a tree describing the construction of scaffolding.
```{julia}
scaffolding = (context(), region, (context(), time_axis, lines) ) ;
```

# Drawing the underlying scaffolding
@fig-scaffolding illustrates the underlying scaffolding for (almost) all our diagrams:
```{julia}
#| label: fig-scaffolding
#| fig-cap: "Scaffolding"
compose(context(units=coordinates), scaffolding)
```

# Colour and line-width for different kinds of incident
Here are dictionaries and variables to hold 
information about various types of incident.
(See <https://juliagraphics.github.io/Colors.jl/stable/namedcolors/>.)
```{julia}
E = epi.AbstractIncident ; A = epi.AbstractInfection ; 
I = epi.Infection ; P = epi.PInfection ; R = epi.Removal ; C = epi.CRemoval

radius   = 0.2cy
smradius = 0.75radius
bit      = -0.02h

col = Dict(
  I => colorant"orange",
  P => colorant"darkgreen",
  R => colorant"tan",
  C => colorant"purple",
  A => colorant"yellow",
  "blank" => colorant"white",
) ;

lw = Dict(
  "bdry"   =>  linewidth(1.00mm),
  "trail"  =>  linewidth(0.75mm),
  "active" =>  linewidth(0.75mm),
  "dormant" => linewidth(0.25mm),
) ;
```

Here is a function which creates a union of all composite types
below a given (typically abstract!) type. This is applied to create
a union type for composite types implementing `AbstractIncident`:
we do this in order to be programmatic about constructing generalized 
drawing functions later.
```{julia}
function unionize_composites(a::Type)::Type
  xl = Type[x for x in subtypes(a)]
  if length(xl) == 0
    return a # a composite type
  else
    xl = Type[unionize_composites(y) for y in xl]
    return reduce((t1, t2) -> Union{t1, t2}, xl) # a union type
  end
end

BasicIncident = unionize_composites(epi.AbstractIncident)
BasicIncident == Union{epi.Removal, epi.CRemoval, epi.Infection, epi.PInfection}
```

# An innovation for an unconditioned \(SIR\) epidemic
We introduce some content by considering potential incidents underlying
an unconditional epidemic.
```{julia}
env0 = epi.Innovation(5, 
  A[
    I(0.11,2,3), I(0.2,2,5), P(0.4,1,2), I(0.5,2,5), I(0.6,2,4), I(0.85,3,4), 
    I(0.9,2,3), I(1.0,2,5), I(1.05,4,5), I(1.2,2,4), I(1.6,3,5), I(1.5,3,4)
    ], 
  R[R(0.3,5), R(0.42,3), R(0.7,3), R(0.55,3), R(0.95,5), R(1.4,2), R(1.55,1),
    R(1.85,2)],
  C[C(1.3,2), C(0.8,1), C(1.7,4), C(1.8,4), C(1.92,5)]
) ;
```

Here are functions which draw inactive respectively active nodes for each of a list
of a given composite type of `BasicIncident`. Variants are added
to deal with `AbstractIncident[]` vectors to do nothing -- this is useful if a
selected sublist is empty as it then becomes an `AbstractIncident[]` vector.
```{julia}
function sketch_incident(incl::Vector{T}) where T <: BasicIncident
  I = eltype(incl) ;
  (context(),
    (context(),
      text([(inc.t)cx for inc in incl],
           [(inc.target)cy for inc in incl], 
           [string(inc) for inc in incl],
           [hcenter], [vcenter]), fontsize(5pt), font("Helvetica")),
    (context(),
      circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in incl if isa(inc, I)], 
             [(inc.target)cy for inc in incl if isa(inc, I)],
             [radius]), fill(col["blank"]), stroke(col[I])), 
  )
end

function sketch_incident(incl::Vector{T}) where T <: epi.AbstractIncident
end

function sketch_realized(incl::Vector{T}) where T <: BasicIncident
  inctype = eltype(incl) ;
  (context(),
    (context(),
      circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in incl if isa(inc, inctype)], 
             [(inc.target)cy for inc in incl if isa(inc, inctype)],
             [radius]), lw["active"], 
             fill(col[inctype]), fillopacity(0.2), stroke(col[inctype]) ),
    if inctype <: epi.AbstractInfection
      (context(),
        circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in active if isa(inc, inctype)], 
               [inc.infectee for inc in active if isa(inc, inctype)],
               [smradius]), lw["active"], 
               fill(col[inctype]), fillopacity(0.5), stroke(col[inctype]) )
    end
  )
end ;

function sketch_realized(incl::Vector{T}) where T <: epi.AbstractIncident
end

function sketch_connections(incl::Vector{T}; active=false) where T <: BasicIncident
  inctype = eltype(incl)
  (context(), 
    (context(), 
      line([[((inc.t)cx, (inc.target)cy+radius), ((inc.t)cx, (inc.infectee)cy)]
             for inc in incl]),
      line([[((inc.t)cx - 0.3bit, (inc.infectee)cy-bit), 
             ((inc.t)cx,          (inc.infectee)cy), 
             ((inc.t)cx + 0.3bit, (inc.infectee)cy-bit)]
             for inc in incl]), stroke(col[inctype]),
             (active ? lw["active"] : lw["dormant"]))
#    (context(),
#      circle([(inc.t)cx for inc in active if isa(inc, inctype)], 
#             [inc.infectee for inc in active if isa(inc, inctype)],
#             [smradius]), lw["active"], 
#             fill(col[I]), fillopacity(0.5), stroke(col[inctype]) ),
  )
end

function sketch_connections(incl::Vector{T}; active=false) where T <: epi.AbstractIncident
end
```

We now add graphical depictions of the potential incidents supplied by the innovation.
Elements are plotted in reverse-order: for example, the first in sequence overlays 
all subsequent elements. @fig-potential illustrates the required plot.
```{julia}
#| label: fig-potential
#| fig-cap: "Potential incidents, including both removals and infections:                                 \
#|           Potential removals (R for _removal_) are indicated by disks with blue outlines,              \
#|           conditional removals (C for _conditioned_) are indicated by disks with purple outlines,      \
#|           potential infections (I for _infected_) are indicated by disks with orange outlines,         \
#|           perpetuated infections (P for _perpetuated_) are indicated by disks with dark green outlines.\
#|           Orange arrows indicate connections of potential infector time-lines                          \
#|           to corresponding potential infectee time-lines.                                              \
#|           Each disk is annotated by the summary description of the corresponding incident.             "

#element_list = Any[context()]
#append!(element_list, [epi.Removal, epi.CRemoval, epi.Infection, epi.PInfection])
#println(Tuple(x for x in element_list))
  


elements = (context(),
  sketch_incident([inc for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, I)]),
  sketch_incident([inc for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, P)]),
  sketch_incident([inc for inc in env0.removals   if isa(inc, R)]),
  sketch_incident([inc for inc in env0.cremovals  if isa(inc, C)]),
  sketch_connections([inc for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, I)]),
  sketch_connections([inc for inc in env0.infections if isa(inc, P)]),
  )
compose(context(units=coordinates), elements, scaffolding)
```

# Evolving the epidemic in process time
Next we must plot the course of epidemics arising from the time-sequence `chron` of potential incidents
supplied by the innovation. The time sequence is derived from the innovation
by the `chronology` function, and we need to compute the trajectory,
and history of realized incidents, corresponding to a specific initial state at time \(0.0\),
given by an `SIR` structure. Application of `evolution_recurse!`,
working destructively on the input lists, delivers the \(SIR\) trajectory `traj`,
and lists realized incidents in `active`.

::: {.callout-caution}
Produce a function calling `evolution_recurse!` which is non-destructive of its arguments!
:::

First of all, we use the `traj` argument to produce a plot against time of the numbers of
susceptibles, infectives and removed individuals. We begin by generating a dataframe
recording the trajectories as the knots of piecewise constant functions.
```{julia}
t1     = 2.0                       # Final time
initial= epi.SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)     # Initial state
states = [initial]                 # Starting state list (will be overwritten)
chron  = epi.chronology(env0)      # Empty list (will be overwritten)
traj, active = epi.evolution_recurse!(states, epi.AbstractIncident[], t1, chron)

using DataFrames
t = [state.t for state in traj]
push!(t, t1)
t = repeat(t, inner=2)[2:(end-1)]
s = repeat([state.s for state in traj], inner=2)
i = repeat([state.i for state in traj], inner=2)
r = repeat([state.r for state in traj], inner=2)
realized = DataFrame(t=t, Susceptibles=s, Infectives=i, Removals=r) ;
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: "Trajectories in process time of susceptibles, infectives (brown dashed line) and removals (grey dotted line)."   

inf_layer = Gadfly.layer(realized, x=:t, y=:Infectives, color=[col[I]], 
  Gadfly.Geom.line, Gadfly.style(line_width=1mm, line_style=[:solid]))
rem_layer = Gadfly.layer(realized, x=:t, y=:Removals, color=[col[R]], 
  Gadfly.Geom.line, 
  Gadfly.style(line_width=1mm, line_style=[:dash]))
sus_layer = Gadfly.layer(realized, x=:t, y=:Susceptibles, color=[colorant"grey"], 
  Gadfly.Geom.line, 
  Gadfly.style(line_width=1mm, line_style=[:dot]))
Gadfly.plot(sus_layer, rem_layer, inf_layer,
  Gadfly.style(panel_fill=colorant"bisque"),
  Gadfly.Guide.xlabel("process time"), 
  Gadfly.Guide.ylabel("removals, infectives, susceptibles", orientation=:vertical))
```

Secondly we can examine which of the potential incidents have been realized. 
We do this by amending @fig-potential so that realized incident nodes have light-coloured backgrounds and 
thicker line-widths, producing @fig-realized. **Need to return a `no-op` 
if the argument is an empty list!?!**

```{julia}
#| label: fig-realized
#| fig-cap: "@fig-potential with epidemic and removal curves: realized incident nodes have  \
#|           light-coloured backgrounds and realized infections have thicker line-widths.   \
#|           The epidemic and removal curves are drawn as thick yellow and brown lines      \
#|           respectively, with regions of infection and removal shaded as yellow and brown \
#|           respectively. Dotted vertical lines connect removal incidents to relevant      \
#|           time-lines, if the removal incident does not already lie on the time-line."

active_removals   = [inc for inc in active if (isa(inc, R) || isa(inc, C))]
observed_removals = [(k, inc) for (k, inc) in enumerate(active_removals) 
                       if k + initial.r < inc.target]

removal_connections = (context(),
  (context(),          # Connecting removal nodes
    circle([(inc.t)cx for (k, inc) in observed_removals], 
           [(k + initial.r)cy for (k, inc) in observed_removals],
           [smradius]), stroke(col[C]), 
           lw["active"], fill(col[C]), fillopacity(0.5) ),
  (context(),          # Connecting removal lines
    line([[((inc.t)cx, (inc.target)cy - radius), 
           ((inc.t)cx, (k + initial.r)cy + radius)]
      for (k, inc) in observed_removals]), 
    stroke(col[R]), lw["trail"], strokedash([0.5mm, 0.5mm]) )
)

realized = (context(),
  sketch_connections([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, I)]; active=true),
  sketch_connections([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, P)]; active=true),
  [context(), sketch_realized([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, I)]),
  sketch_realized([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, P)]),
  sketch_realized([inc for inc in active if isa(inc, C)]),]
)

removed_fill = [(a,b) for (a,b) in zip(t, r) if b>0]
push!(removed_fill, (t1, 1))
infected_fill = [(a,b) for (a,b) in zip(t, i+r) if b>0]
append!(infected_fill, reverse(removed_fill))
timelines = (context(),
  (context(),          # Removed trail
    line([(a,b) for (a,b) in zip(t, r) if b>0]),
    stroke(col[R]), lw["bdry"] ),
  (context(),          # Removed trail
    polygon(removed_fill),
    fill(col[R]), fillopacity(0.1) ),
  (context(),          # Epidemic trail
    line([zip(t, i+r)]),
    stroke(col[A]), lw["bdry"] ),
  (context(),          # Epidemic trail
    polygon(infected_fill),
    fill(col[A]), fillopacity(0.1) ),
)

compose(context(units=coordinates), removal_connections, realized, 
           elements, timelines, scaffolding)
```
